editorial_notes: The movement lemma1450 prints id:P->P. That literal identity would make every fiber a singleton and every face both lower and upper, so it is not the map used by the ensuing argument. Lines1463–1464 require an edge parallel to e_i to be vertical, and1474–1475 require line-segment fibers. These uniquely specify the affine-span quotient along span(e_i), up to affine coordinates in the quotient, with height psi=<x,e_i>. Retain the printed id and disclose this reading; no new movement proof is inserted.

With the definitions1509, r_t counts right-leaning leaves minus k and l_t counts left-leaning leaves minus k. The original contraction recipe1513 gives dim F_t=r_t and dim G_t=l_t. The displays1509 and1522–1524 exchange these two letters. The recipe, author formulas and proof are retained; the letter convention just stated is the one compatible with the construction and with the inequality r_s+l_t<=d used there.

The edge-direction calculation877 has the dot-product difference reversed: the displayed earlier +x/later -x edge pairs as x(v_i-v_(i+j))>0. The consecutive-difference sum at888 also has its initial index offset: the source basis886 gives a_(p+q-1)-a_p for coordinates p+1,...,p+q-1, with endpoint coefficients0. These are source-determined sign/index readings; the equal-or-zero coefficient argument is unchanged. At1437 the edge is indeed a positive multiple of e_i, but the scalar is the product of the total weights of the two outside subtrees, not in general the product of two individual leaf weights. The subsequent movement proof uses only positive parallelism. Preserve all printed formulas; do not certify the printed scalar as an exact general value.

At1005 the right-hand map on the lower faces of tilde P is pr, as fixed by the domains and factorization978–982 and the immediately following sentence; tilde-pi has domain Q. This is a cellwise affine homeomorphism on the lower graph, not a claim that the entire piecewise-linear graph is one affine subspace. The original display is retained.

The boundary sentence1651 is compressed. Its order-theoretic input is the classical Tamari face-interval property explicitly listed in standard_prerequisites. It applies to the s<=t<u vertices and B=G_t intersect G_u from the author preceding construction; the conclusion also uses the already proved tightness and full dimension of the current maximal cell. This is an explanation of the scope of the omitted classical convex/order step, not a replacement author proof. The specialized neighbor classification and propagation remain solution obligations.

The counted formula has n>=2 as in582–584; the arity-one operadic unit635 is a separate convention, not an n-2=-1 instance. In product-facet induction omit point factors when choosing a facet and apply the Boolean-fiber facet argument only in positive dimension. The author treats dimensions0 and1 separately at1529; no facet-containing-vertex assertion for a point is made.

source_issues.explanation: For id:P->P, every fiber is a singleton, tilde P is the graph of psi, and every face is both lower and upper. Thus1450 cannot literally yield1451-1459. The subsequent author argument1463-1464 requires an e_i-parallel edge to be vertical in a fiber, and1474-1475 requires each fiber to be a line segment whose non-endpoints are not vertices. Together with psi=<x,e_i>, these specify projection along span(e_i), unique up to an affine change of the quotient coordinates. Take the quotient of the affine span of P by this line (equivalently its orthogonal projection), and identify P with its lifted graph tilde P. All remaining printed steps then have their stated meaning: connected lower/upper complexes, no vertical crossing edge, every vertex an endpoint, and relative-face movement. A visible note must say exactly this; retain the original id display and do not claim it is true literally.
source_issues.disposition: Resolved/disclosed by reviews/A-2039-associahedral-magic-formula/C-independent-r002.json; focused migration retains required visible notes.

source_issues.explanation: With the definitions at1509, r_t counts right-leaning leaves minus k and l_t counts left-leaning leaves minus k. The actual construction1513 contracts LEFT-leaning internal edges to form F_t and RIGHT-leaning internal edges to form G_t; the same sentence counts these as r_t and l_t respectively. Hence dim F_t=r_t and dim G_t=l_t. The displayed1509 and1522-1524 interchange these letters. Since L counts right-leaning interior leaves, L(s)<=L(t) gives r_s<=r_t and therefore r_s+l_t<=d, the exact inequality needed in the matching argument. Already for the two vertices of the segment K3, the minimum has r=0,l=1, F_min a point and G_min the segment. The original contraction recipe is correct and uniquely fixes the labels; it must not be reversed to fit the erroneous dimension display.

source_issues.explanation: The author1651 asserts beta(H) is not in the boundary without expanding the step. Here B=G_t intersect G_u is a facet of G_t, u belongs to B by the original contraction description1627, and t is not in B because min G_u=u>t. If beta(H) lay in a facet Q of K, its exposing functional would force both F_s and B into Q. Thus s,u are in Q. The classical Tamari face-interval property then gives t in Q from s<=t<u. Since B is a facet of G_t and t lies outside B, the affine hull of B and t is aff(G_t), so Q would contain all of G_t. This would put beta(F_s times G_t) in the boundary, contradicting its full dimension and the already established tightness. This is a reviewer verification of the author compressed convex/order step. Name the classical interval fact explicitly; do not insert this paragraph as author prose or give the magical formula itself as a background theorem.
